summary: BridgeVM presents a QEMU virt-compatible guest contract so stock ArmVirtQemu firmware and stock Windows 11 ARM media work unmodified. It is not bit-identical. Every known deviation is listed here.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Writing device status zero resets guest-programmed device state for a new negotiation.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Status-zero MMIO and legacy PCI resets clear driver features, both feature selectors, queue selector and legacy page size along with queue state. Backend configuration and request statistics are retained.
deviations.impact: Resolved: stale guest negotiation state no longer survives a device reset. The reset path adds only scalar stores and leaves request processing unchanged.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Writable fw_cfg entry DMA behavior is defined by the entry callback.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: A DMA write exceeding the selected writable entry's remaining capacity returns DMA_CTL_ERROR before reading any payload, without changing the entry or cursor.
deviations.impact: Oversized requests cannot cause millions of guest-memory probes. The firmware ramfb write of 28 bytes at offset zero still succeeds.

deviations.qemu_behavior: ramfb geometry and host capture allocation limits depend on the display backend.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Shared ramfb sizing rejects stride times height above 64 MiB with SizeOverflow before allocation, matching the interactive display export ceiling.
deviations.impact: Snapshot and telemetry callers receive an error for oversized guest geometry rather than allocating or panicking. Supported display geometry is unchanged.

deviations.qemu_behavior: The 2D max_hostmem budget accounts for host pixel storage.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: The existing 256 MiB cumulative 2D budget also counts retained backing-entry capacity. Attachments reaching the limit return ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY without changing the prior backing. 3D backing is unchanged.
deviations.impact: Many small resources cannot bypass the host-memory limit with large backing lists. Normal attachments and replacement of existing backing remain supported.

deviations.qemu_behavior: UDP receive buffering depends on the selected network backend.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: NAT UDP polling stops at the existing 10000-frame reply queue limit and resumes receiving after the queue drains, retaining edge-triggered readiness.
deviations.impact: Under sustained overload UDP datagrams may be dropped by the host socket buffer rather than consuming unbounded host memory. Ordinary datagrams are unchanged.

deviations.qemu_behavior: The caller supplies a writable firmware variable store and boot options.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Disk import without vars captures a recognized managed pair's current disk and vars under native ownership; unmanaged disks use the bundled Windows seed and install-time GPT ESP boot-entry seeding on the imported RAW copy. Supplied vars remain byte-identical. Missing GPT or ESP retains the plain seed with a nonblocking Korean notice.
deviations.impact: A new variable store does not preserve custom boot options or another machine's TPM identity. MBR/BIOS disks cannot gain UEFI boot support from seeding and may reach the firmware shell instead of Windows.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU has no BridgeVM DISPLAYMODE or BVDISPLAY guest-agent protocol.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: BVDISPLAY adds virtio=found|none for whether Windows EnumDisplayDevices exposes a 1AF4:1050 display adapter. The host treats an absent or unknown field as unknown. With the saved display-driver-installed flag and virtio=none, the VM window offers one dismissible diagnostic per run without clearing the flag, retrying or blocking commands.
deviations.impact: A staged driver that did not bind no longer silently hides the display notice; Windows Device Manager is the suggested next action. This reports the display adapter, not driver-store installation status.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Userspace-modelled GICv3 with fully observable distributor, redistributor and CPU interface state, and observable timer interrupt delivery.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Apple Hypervisor.framework in-kernel GIC. Redistributor and CPU interface state is only reachable from the owning vCPU thread, and virtual timer interrupts are delivered by the framework without producing a guest exit.
deviations.impact: Timer delivery cannot be observed through exit counters, so vtimer_exits is 0 on both passing and stalling boots. Cancellation and timer masking were investigated in historical A1 stalls; current A1 state and later gate evidence are recorded in capabilities/windows-hvf.json.

deviations.qemu_behavior: GICv3 with ITS available for MSI translation.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: MSI support follows Apple's GIC frame rather than a QEMU-identical ITS. In the native backend a nonzero hv_gic_send_msi result triggers the existing fatal lifecycle stop; the linked entry specifies the advertised frame/range and retained failure fields. The optional userspace backend is unchanged.
deviations.impact: Devices must use the advertised MSI path; a QEMU-identical ITS layout is unsupported. Invalid guest-programmable MSI operands can also trigger fatal provider rejection. Raw status alone is not a cause diagnosis; the run does not automatically retry or ignore the failure. Evidence is deterministic injected-provider testing only, without live guest compatibility proof.

deviations.qemu_behavior: virtio-gpu with virglrenderer over a host OpenGL/Vulkan stack.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: virtio-gpu with a Venus path onto MoltenVK/Metal, plus BridgeVM's own scanout and present handling.
deviations.impact: The guest sees an experimental Vulkan path and an experimental D3D11-compatible subset through DXVK. Five DXVK features are relaxed rather than implemented, so full D3D11 conformance is not claimed.

deviations.qemu_behavior: TPM backend over the host swtpm socket, configured by the operator.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Bundled signed swtpm with BridgeVM-owned identity, export and recovery lifecycle keyed to the Keychain.
deviations.impact: Windows sees a working TPM 2.0, but VM portability follows BridgeVM's lifecycle rules rather than a portable QEMU TPM state directory.

deviations.qemu_behavior: SMCCC TRNG backed by the host entropy source when advertised.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Arm DEN 0098 v1.0 served from the macOS CSPRNG through SecRandomCopyBytes, with no fallback: provider failure returns NO_ENTROPY and a platform without a provider returns NOT_SUPPORTED. BridgeVM additionally accepts a zero-bit request with SUCCESS, zero data and no provider call; DEN 0098 defines the request domain starting at one bit. GET_UUID identifies the implementation-chosen SecRandomCopyBytes backend association, not a universal service UUID.
deviations.impact: Resolved. The earlier implementation derived output from the vCPU exit counter, which a guest can approximate, while advertising the service as supported. Images created before the fix remain classified pre-secure-trng-development-only.

deviations.qemu_behavior: PSCI 1.1 CPU_ON and AFFINITY_INFO state table and error codes.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: DEN 0022 CPU_ON state table with an atomic Off->OnPending transition, and AFFINITY_INFO that reads the X2 affinity level and searches the whole topology including CPU0.
deviations.impact: Resolved. CPU_ON previously reported ALREADY_ON for a merely pending CPU, and AFFINITY_INFO ignored X2 while collapsing OnPending and unknown targets into OFF, so a conforming guest could read incorrect CPU state.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Not applicable; QEMU does not define Windows composition behaviour.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Windows composes titles through DWM as Composed: Flip. No client has reached Hardware: Independent Flip on this driver.
deviations.impact: The linked historical measurement was approximately 20 FPS against the unchanged 30 FPS gate. Later A3 evidence and current state are recorded in capabilities/windows-hvf.json; composed presentation is not itself an open-criterion claim.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Under HVF the guest counter stops while the Mac sleeps, and QEMU leaves the guest clock behind until the guest's own time sync; only a management layer can set it (guest-set-time).
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: When the host wall clock moves more than 2 s beyond the monotonic clock between service ticks (a host sleep), the resident agent service runs one Set-Date to the host's UTC time. The same resync runs at each boot's first service start and after a VM pause, and first sets Windows to the Mac's time zone (mapped through the app's CLDR table) when they differ; a running VM checks the Mac's zone once a minute. The PL031 counter follows the host wall clock, as QEMU's default -rtc clock=host.
deviations.impact: The Windows clock is correct again shortly after the Mac wakes instead of lagging by the sleep time for up to a week. Without the agent service the clock stays behind until Windows syncs or reboots.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU 11.0.2's NVMe device advertises Dataset Management with Write Zeroes, Compare and Copy (ONCS), DLFEAT 0x9 (a deallocated block reads zeros; Write Zeroes may deallocate) and range limits in the NVM Identify Controller page (DMRL, DMRSL, DMSL). A range outside the namespace or over DMRSL is skipped and the command still succeeds. With discard=unmap a file-backed drive punches holes aligned to the host file-system block (F_PUNCHHOLE on macOS); with the default discard=ignore nothing is freed (hw/nvme/ctrl.c, hw/nvme/ns.c, block/file-posix.c).
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: ONCS advertises Dataset Management only. DLFEAT stays 0, so what a deallocated block reads is not reported, and the NVM Identify Controller page stays zero: no range limits besides NR's 256 ranges and the namespace. Deallocate punches the whole host file-system blocks inside each range out of a raw write-back image (F_PUNCHHOLE on macOS); partial blocks at a range's edges keep their bytes, and memory disks, read-only overlays and file systems that cannot punch (HFS+, exFAT) complete the command unchanged. A range ending past the namespace, its start plus length overflowing included, fails the whole command with LBA Out of Range (DNR) before anything is punched; reserved bits above NR fail it with Invalid Field (DNR).
deviations.impact: Windows' TRIM (file deletes and Optimize-Volume -ReTrim) gives the space back to the Mac when the image is on APFS. A deallocated block then reads zeros where it was punched and its old data elsewhere, which DLFEAT 0 allows and NTFS never reads. A malformed range list is refused instead of partly ignored. The punches run on the doorbell vCPU's NVMe worker without the platform lock, and a write fetched after a deallocation and overlapping it waits for its punch (inline under the lock when BRIDGEVM_NVME_UNLOCKED_IO=0 or checkpointing); the final report's nvme dsm: record counts their time.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU virt (11.0) describes \_SB.GED_ (ACPI0013) with an edge-triggered SPI 9 interrupt and a 32-bit read-to-clear event selector at 0x0908_0000. Its _EVT notifies \_SB.PWRB (PNP0C0C, _UID 0) on the power-down event and \_SB.ERR0 (PNP0C33) on the generic-error event. system_powerdown sets the selector bit and pulses the line.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Same GED name, _HID, _UID, address, SPI, edge flag, selector semantics, power-down bit (0x2) and _EVT shape. Differences: only the power-down event exists, with no generic-error branch and no ERR0 device. The line stays high until the guest reads the selector and is re-raised on each press, instead of a pulse. PWRB keeps its EISAID-encoded _HID and has no _UID. The host trigger is a POWERBUTTON line in the live input control file.
deviations.impact: The host gets a shutdown request that does not depend on the guest agent, for example at the login screen or with a hung agent; the guest applies its own power-button action. A guest that configures the line as edge-triggered cannot tell the held line from a pulse, and the held line still delivers the event if the GIC treats it as level-triggered.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU virt (11.0) describes no battery or AC adapter; an Arm guest sees no power source.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: When the Mac has an internal battery (or BRIDGEVM_HVF_FAKE_BATTERY is set for a test), the DSDT adds \_SB.ADP0 (ACPI0003, _PSR, _PCL) and \_SB.BAT0 (PNP0C0A, _UID 1, _STA, _BIF, _BST, _PCL). Their methods read ten 32-bit registers of a read-only page at 0x090C_0000 (OperationRegion BATR, 0x28 bytes, DWordAcc); guest writes are ignored. The GED _EVT notifies them on three BridgeVM selector bits: 0x10000 when the adapter state changes (Notify ADP0, 0x80), 0x20000 when _BST changes (Notify BAT0, 0x80) and 0x40000 when _STA or _BIF changes (Notify BAT0, 0x81). _BIF reports mWh with a fixed 60 Wh design and full-charge capacity and 11.4 V; _BST takes the remaining capacity from the Mac's percent and the rate from macOS' time estimates (0xFFFFFFFF while macOS calculates). The probe re-reads the Mac on macOS' power-source notification and at least every 30 s. Until the running guest agent's READY says onbattery (its scheduled task keeps running on battery) and any update that brought it is confirmed, a Mac on battery is shown on AC and not charging, with the Mac's percentage: Task Scheduler does not start an older agent's task on battery, and the update that fixes the task comes through that agent. Without a Mac battery the DSDT is unchanged and the page is unmapped.
deviations.impact: Windows on a MacBook can show the Mac's charge and whether it is plugged in, so its power plan, battery saver and apps can adapt. Capacity in Wh and the voltage are synthetic: powercfg /batteryreport shows 60 Wh, not the Mac's battery. Evidence is deterministic AML, page, platform and host-reading tests, iasl and acpiexec checks of the DSDT, and one operator run per arm on a Mac without a battery using the test override (2026-11-11): Windows 11 bound both devices, Win32_Battery and powercfg /batteryreport showed the battery, and an unplug reached Windows (GED events 0x30000). That run also showed the guest agent's scheduled task stopping on battery under Task Scheduler's defaults; the task now says false to both battery settings, and an agent update re-registers older tasks. A later run showed an older agent never starting when Windows booted on battery, which the AC hold until onbattery addresses.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU has no shared-folder guest-agent Explorer integration of its own.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: New Windows registrations opt in to a dedicated Mac folder created at first launch; existing registrations and clones stay unchanged. When sharing requests a listing of an existing guest folder, the agent attempts Shell.Application pintohome once, recording the attempt under ProgramData/BridgeVM before invoking the verb. No READY capability is added. Failure logs one guest-agent line without failing the host request; a later manual unpin is respected.
deviations.impact: The shared folder is offered in Explorer Quick Access without re-pinning on every boot; live verification of the elevated interactive-task Shell context is required.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU has no shared-folder guest-agent push protocol of its own.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: READY putmtime promises that PUT, PUTEND and LPUTEND apply the optional host millisecond timestamp. The host accepts a post-push listing as its write only when size and the sent timestamp match, including the zero sub-millisecond ticks. Without the marker the old size-only adoption remains.
deviations.impact: A same-size Windows edit before the first post-push listing is fetched instead of silently adopted as the Mac write.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU has no shared-folder guest-agent listing protocol of its own.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Recursive shared-folder directory rows keep isDir=1 and use size=1 for a reparse point (ordinary directories remain size=0). The host holds that name and subtree unseen until a later listing reports an ordinary directory or removes it. Older hosts ignore directory sizes; older agents leave the previous behavior unchanged.
deviations.impact: A Windows junction cannot turn an unvisited subtree into deletions on the Mac, and sync never transfers through it.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU has no Windows clipboard integration of its own; only a guest agent or remote-display protocol can share one.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: With clipboard sync on and an agent that answers CLIPCAPS with IMAGE_PNG, the resident agent service also moves clipboard images: a Mac copy holding public.png or public.tiff becomes one Windows clipboard write of the copy's text, a bitmap and the PNG format, and a Windows bitmap or PNG copy becomes public.png on the Mac. Images over 32 MiB or 16384 pixels per side stay where they were copied. An older agent keeps text-only sync.
deviations.impact: Screenshots and copied images paste across in either direction. A Finder file copy is not an image copy, so its icon is never sent.
